prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas for Trying to Beat the S&P 500

No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500 over a single year. Most professional fund managers fail to beat it, and over one year luck matters more than skill. My information also only runs to about mid-2026, so I don't know current prices, valuations, or recent earnings. Treat this list as a starting point for your own research, not as advice fitted to your finances.

## The list

I aimed for quality companies across different sectors so the portfolio isn't just one AI bet.

| # | Ticker | Company | Sector | Why it could outperform | Key risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MSFT | Microsoft | Tech | Growth in its Azure cloud and earning money from AI; steady, recurring enterprise revenue | Heavy AI spending may not pay off |
| 2 | GOOGL | Alphabet | Communication | Search, YouTube and Cloud; its Gemini AI and Waymo self-driving cars could add upside; historically cheaper than its big-tech peers | AI chatbots taking search traffic; antitrust rulings |
| 3 | AMZN | Amazon | Consumer/Tech | AWS cloud plus a fast-growing, high-margin advertising business | Heavy spending; weaker consumer demand |
| 4 | TSM | Taiwan Semiconductor | Semiconductors | Makes most of the world's leading-edge chips, including AI chips | China–Taiwan tensions; tariffs |
| 5 | AVGO | Broadcom | Semiconductors | Custom AI chips and networking gear, plus VMware software revenue | Relies on a few big customers; high valuation |
| 6 | LLY | Eli Lilly | Healthcare | Leader in obesity and diabetes drugs (GLP-1s), with a strong pipeline | Drug-price pressure; competition; high valuation |
| 7 | JPM | JPMorgan Chase | Financials | Best-in-class bank that earns well across interest-rate environments | Loan losses in a recession |
| 8 | V | Visa | Financials | Takes a small cut of a huge volume of payments, with very high margins | Regulation; new payment methods |
| 9 | GEV | GE Vernova | Industrials | Sells gas turbines and grid equipment into rising electricity demand from data centers | Stock has already risen a lot; cyclical business |
| 10 | BRK.B | Berkshire Hathaway | Diversified | Stabilizer with a large cash pile that tends to hold up in downturns | Lags in strong bull markets; management change after Buffett |

About 8 of these are already among the largest S&P 500 holdings, so this portfolio is essentially a concentrated, quality-focused version of the index. It won't beat the index by a huge margin, but it's also less likely to badly trail it. If you want a bigger chance of beating the index, you would need smaller or less-owned stocks, which also carry a bigger chance of losing to it.

## How to use it sensibly

- **Core and satellite:** Keep most of your money (e.g., 70–90%) in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund, and put a smaller portion into picks like these. This limits the damage if your picks lag.
- **Check before buying:** Look at each stock's current valuation compared with its growth, its latest earnings, and any news since mid-2026.
- **Size equally and set rules:** Put roughly the same amount in each stock, and decide in advance when you'd sell or rebalance.
- **Consider costs:**
  - Taxes on short-term gains.
  - If you invest from outside the US, currency moves and withholding tax on dividends.
- **Judge fairly:** Compare your total return, including dividends, against the S&P 500's total return, not just its price change.

If you'd like, I can write a script that tracks this portfolio against the S&P 500 or tests different weightings, using price data you provide.
